table.step: Setup / definitions (tables, marks, start states, rounding)
table.ruleA: Six stages 1..6; rated 10,8,12,6,9,7; upper 7,6,9,5,7,5; lower 3,2,4,2,3,2; start 3,6,6,2,2,1; all CLEAR; ground total 0; chain limit 38; quarter/half rounded down (floor).
table.ruleB: Six teams 1..6; WIP 10,8,12,6,9,7; upper 7,6,9,5,7,5; lower 3,2,4,2,3,2; start 3,6,6,2,2,1; all ROUTINE; closed tally 0; target 38; divisions floor (7/4=1, 9/2=4).

table.ruleA: Add the cycle's input row to each stage; rated charge not enforced.
table.ruleB: Add the sprint's New Tickets row to each team; WIP limit not enforced.

table.ruleA: Sequential in order 1..6; if charge > rated (strict), excess = charge - rated goes to stage n+1 and stage set to rated; equal or less: nothing. Stage 1's excess is already in stage 2 when stage 2 is handled (cascade). Stage 6 excess to ground.
table.ruleB: Sequential in order 1..6; if open > WIP (strict), excess to team n+1 and team set to WIP; equal or less: nothing. Excess reaches next team before it is handled (cascade). Team 6 excess closed and tallied.

table.ruleA: Read charge after Step 2. CLEAR and charge >= upper -> ASSERTED; ASSERTED and charge <= lower -> CLEAR; otherwise unchanged; at most one change per cycle; log (cycle, stage, before, after).
table.ruleB: Read count after step 2. ROUTINE and count >= upper -> ESCALATED; ESCALATED and count <= lower -> ROUTINE; otherwise unchanged; at most one change per sprint; log (sprint, team, before, after).

table.ruleA: Amounts computed from each stage's charge at start of step using post-Step-3 state: CLEAR floor(q/4), ASSERTED floor(q/2). All six computed before any change, applied simultaneously. Each stage reduced by own amount; CLEAR amount to ground; ASSERTED amount added to stage n-1; stage 1 ASSERTED amount to ground. No rated enforcement; overflow waits for next cycle's Step 2 (never handled after cycle 5).
table.ruleB: Amounts from count at start of step using status: ROUTINE floor(t/4), ESCALATED floor(t/2). All computed before any change, applied at once; bounced tickets do not change already-computed amounts. ROUTINE amount closed; ESCALATED amount bounced to team n-1; team 1 ESCALATED amount closed. No WIP enforcement; excess handled next sprint's step 2, never after sprint 5.

table.ruleA: Sum all six. If total > 38 (strict; 38 does not trip), every stage (all six) becomes floor(q/2); removed charge (q - floor(q/2)) to ground; log cycle. Else nothing.
table.ruleB: Sum all six. If total > 38 (strict; 38 does nothing), every team (all six) becomes floor(t/2); removed tickets closed and tallied; log sprint. Else nothing.

table.ruleA: After Step 5 of cycle 5: end charges 1..6, end states, all state changes in order, trip cycles (or none), ground total, balance check (start + inputs = end + ground).
table.ruleB: After step 5 of sprint 5: end counts 1..6, end statuses, all status changes in order, halving sprints (or none), closed tally, balance check (start + inputs = end + closed).

result.probeWhy: I chose it by searching for an input that hits every boundary where a reworded rule could split the two documents: a multi-stage cascade inside Step 2 (stage n's excess pushes n+1 over), stage 6 overflow to ground/closed, a charge exactly equal to an upper mark while CLEAR (tests >= vs >), exactly equal to a lower mark while ASSERTED (tests <= vs <), stage 1 ASSERTED with a nonzero amount (tests where its feedback goes), a cycle whose post-Step-4 total is exactly 38 (tests strict > on the halving), halving on odd quantities (tests floor and what goes to ground), and an end stage left above its rating by feedback in cycle 5 (tests non-enforcement after the last cycle). Note: the printed tables also happen to hit all of these, so they are a stronger test than they look. I also ran a random check of 300,000 starting/input tables (0-9) through two separately written implementations, with 0 mismatches.
result.differingRule: None. Once the names are mapped (stage=team, charge=open tickets, rated charge=WIP limit, CLEAR=ROUTINE, ASSERTED=ESCALATED, ground=closed tally, breaker trip=backlog halving), every rule matches, including order, thresholds, rounding, where amounts go and timing.
result.trust: Both routes find SAME, so I have no conflict to settle. The two routes back each other up. The table compares the documents clause by clause. The probe and a random check of 300,000 tables run through two separately written implementations, with 0 mismatches.
